Nxeon hosting platform, Next.js/TypeScript/Prisma/Postgres, repo /opt/nxeon (git, branch `main`).

## The ask

The admin portal's "Recent visitors" view (find it — check `lib/admin-groups.ts` for a visitor-analytics nav entry, and `app/admin/` for the actual page; there's a real visitor-device-analytics dashboard already built, per recent work in this codebase) currently shows a list with no pagination — find out how it's limited today (a hard `take: N` on the query, or genuinely unbounded) and add real pagination.

## What to build

- Server-side pagination (page number or cursor-based — match whatever pattern already exists elsewhere in this admin portal for a paginated list, e.g. check the support tickets list, the chat inbox, or the billing/invoices list for an existing pagination convention to copy rather than inventing a new one).
- A simple page-through UI (prev/next, or numbered pages, matching the existing admin design language — look at nearby components before adding new ones).
- Keep existing filters/sorting on the visitors list working correctly alongside pagination.
- Reasonable page size (look at what similar lists in this codebase use as a default, e.g. 25/50 rows, and match it rather than picking an arbitrary number).

## Ground rules

- `cd /opt/nxeon && git worktree add /opt/nxeon-wt-visitorpage -b feature/visitors-pagination`, symlink only `.env`, real `node_modules` via `npm ci`. Check `df -h /` first — if under 5GB free, stop and report. Delete your worktree's `node_modules`/`.next` once committed.
- `npm run build` and `npx tsc --noEmit` must pass clean.
- Commit but do NOT merge to main, do NOT touch staging/production. Low-risk UI change, but stop for a quick review anyway per this session's convention.

Report back: which file(s) you changed, the pagination approach you used and why (matching an existing pattern), the commit hash, and confirmation of disk cleanup.

Trigger whenever the user mentions "deck," "slides," "presentation," or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. If a .pptx or .potx file needs to be opened, created, or touched, use this skill.

You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces — posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, handing the viewer a file to save, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").

TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

Confirmed: main is untouched, work is committed only on `feature/visitors-pagination`, no merge performed.

## Summary

**What I found**: The admin nav entry "Visitors" (`lib/admin-groups.ts`) points to `/opt/nxeon/app/admin/visitors/page.tsx`, which renders two tables. The one with filters/sorting (date range, source kind, sort direction — `components/admin/TrafficFeedFilter.tsx`) is the "Traffic feed" table, backed by `visitFeed()`/`visitFeedCount()` in `lib/analytics.ts`. It was hard-capped at `FEED_LIMIT = 200` (a flat `take: N`, no offset), so any filtered range with more than 200 matches was silently truncated with no way to page further. (The separate "Recent visits" widget above it is a fixed top-40 snapshot with no filters — not this list.)

**Pagination approach**: Copied the existing page-number convention used by `app/admin/invoices/page.tsx` and `app/admin/users/page.tsx` — the shared `paginate()`/`pageHref()` helpers in `lib/pagination.ts`, with the same `PER_PAGE = 25` default those lists use. This is server-side (Prisma `skip`/`take`), driven by a `?page=` query param, with Prev/Next `<Link>` controls and a "Page X of Y · N matching visits" footer, matching the invoices page's layout exactly.

**Files changed** (all in `/opt/nxeon-wt-visitorpage`, branch `feature/visitors-pagination`):
- `lib/analytics.ts` — `visitFeed()` now takes `skip`/`take` (from `paginate()`) instead of a flat `limit`, capped at 500 as before.
- `app/admin/visitors/page.tsx` — computes `pg = paginate(sp, feedTotal, 25)`, fetches the page via `visitFeed({...dateFilter, skip: pg.skip, take: pg.take})`, renders Prev/Next links via `pageHref()` that preserve `from`/`to`/`kind`/`dir`.
- `components/admin/TrafficFeedFilter.tsx` — `apply()` now deletes the `page` param when a new filter is submitted, so a stale page number from before the filter change can't leave the user on an out-of-range page.

**Verification**: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean, `npm run build` exit 0 with no errors.

**Commit**: `ff45a82` on `feature/visitors-pagination`, not merged to `main` (`main` still at `1b33eaa`), staging/production untouched.

**Disk cleanup**: `node_modules` (1.1G) and `.next` (1.4G) removed from the worktree after commit; `/opt/nxeon-wt-visitorpage` is now 35M. `df -h /` shows 20G free (was 22G before `npm ci`, temporarily dropped during build, now reclaimed).
